disclaimer: These pitches are invented parody characters for the comedy-fantasy tower. They are not research facts, not canon, and not Owner-approved. Each one points at a sourced inspiration and then leaves it. None of them uses a worshipped deity as the joke. Child-eating traditions (Lamia, Lamashtu, the ogress side of Baba Yaga) are not pitched.
worldFit: Wild creatures, Corrupted Echoes, and Tower Guardians inside the existing Mysterious Tower. They do not join or rename Aegis Dominion, Phantom Blades, Celestial Nexus, or Sanctuary Order. No combat numbers.

pitches.comedyConcept: A tower-canteen hawk who steals the plate the moment it lands and leaves one ruined crumb with a comment card.
pitches.visualIdentity: Winged server with bird legs, a stained apron, and a tray that is always empty. Ugly cheerful face, not a siren and not a mermaid.
pitches.personality: Helpful in the way a gust is helpful. Apologizes while chewing.
pitches.signatureTrait: Removes one prepared item and replaces it with a smear.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The public-domain harpy snatches food and befouls scraps. Snatchcourse is a canteen employee. No myth name on the card.

pitches.comedyConcept: A three-part choir on bird legs whose hold music is so good that parties forget which floor they wanted.
pitches.visualIdentity: Women's faces and torsos on bird bodies, sheet-music feathers, a mast-and-rope prop they keep trying to tie the listener to. No fish tail.
pitches.personality: Professional, slightly hurt when anyone walks past humming a different song.
pitches.signatureTrait: A song that delays a turn until someone makes a louder noise of their own.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The fetched Greek image is a bird-woman, which already separates her from mermaid characters in modern films.

pitches.thaiName: เรสเซิลเมน
pitches.comedyConcept: A lion who has read the weapon policy and stands in the doorway waiting to be hugged into submission.
pitches.visualIdentity: A huge gold-brown lion in a too-small hi-vis vest. Arrows stick in the vest and fall off the hide. No hero costume beside him.
pitches.personality: Proud, patient, and offended by pointed objects.
pitches.signatureTrait: Strikes glance off. A grapple is the only thing he respects.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The labour is public domain. The character is a safety-vest lion, not a depiction of Heracles.

pitches.creatureType: Hoard-dragon who used to be the payroll clerk
pitches.comedyConcept: He sat on the tower's lost-and-found until the coins grew scales and the scales grew him.
pitches.visualIdentity: A dragon still wearing half a clerk's waistcoat, with a receipt spike for a horn and a stomach that clinks.
pitches.personality: Polite until asked to make change. Then he is a cave.
pitches.signatureTrait: Eating a coin of his hoard teaches a secret and also makes everyone nearby greedier.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The saga dragon guards cursed gold and was once a man. Goldgut is an office hoard. No ring-cycle staging, no named hero, no borrowed dragon silhouette from a film.

pitches.comedyConcept: He does not chase you through a maze. The hallway is his rental unit, and every correct door is listed as occupied.
pitches.visualIdentity: A broad human body, a bull's head with a doorbell for a nose-ring, a ring of keys that are all the same key. Star-shaped brand on the shoulder, not a film minotaur harness.
pitches.personality: Hungry, contractual, and convinced the tribute is a security deposit.
pitches.signatureTrait: The room rotates when he stamps a lease. Offerings calm him; a straight answer does not.
pitches.entranceConcept: A door marked EXIT opens onto the same corridor, and he is already sitting in the new copy.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: Horns wide enough to scrape both walls, keys hanging to the knees.
pitches.signatureMechanic: The battlefield is a loop. A party that backtracks meets a fresher version of the last room.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: When the lease is torn up he drops to all fours and the corridor loses its doors.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: He hands over a key, looks surprised that it fits, and the walls fold flat like a cancelled floor plan.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: Bent keys, a star-shaped nose-ring, a deposit slip that is also a map.
pitches.whyNotACopy: Bull-headed man in a maze is the recognizable public-domain shape. The landlord gag, the doorbell, and the lease are the new identity.

pitches.comedyConcept: A shepherd giant who runs a bed and breakfast inside a floor. The rating is one star because he has one eye and eats guests who mention the sheep.
pitches.visualIdentity: A looming shepherd with a single forehead eye behind a cracked monocle, a wool blanket used as a cape, and a guestbook he cannot read.
pitches.personality: Hospitable until the review is filed. Then the menu changes.
pitches.signatureTrait: Hospitality that becomes a bite if anyone looks at the eye too long or asks for a second blanket.
pitches.entranceConcept: The party wakes already checked in. Breakfast is whatever they were carrying.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: One round eye high on the face, crook bent into a coat hook.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Guest rules. Breaking a posted rule (no staring, no names, no leaving) flips him from host to hunter.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: He closes the cave mouth with a boulder-shaped room service cart.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: The monocle pops, he mistakes his own reflection in a tray for a rival inn, and the party slips out while he argues with it.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A one-star badge, a wool cape, a guestbook with the party's names already wrong.
pitches.whyNotACopy: Uses the sourced one-eyed shepherd who eats guests. Does not restage the 'Nobody' episode, which this research pass did not verify line by line, and does not copy a film Cyclops.

pitches.comedyConcept: Cut one head and two action items grow in its place. The only way to adjourn is to cauterize the minutes.
pitches.visualIdentity: A nine-headed swamp serpent in a conference pond. Each head wears a different lanyard. One head, the middle one, refuses to be minuted and is the chair.
pitches.personality: Every head agrees that the meeting should continue.
pitches.signatureTrait: Severed heads return as two smaller heads unless the stump is sealed.
pitches.entranceConcept: The floor is a marsh with a lectern. A crab with a badge scuttles in as acting secretary.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: A fan of lanyarded necks over a low body, one neck taller in the center.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Head count is a resource. Reducing it without sealing it increases the number of attacks.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: The immortal middle head is buried under a rock of unfinished business and keeps speaking from underneath.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: Iolaus is not present. A player spends a seal, the necks go out like candles, and the crab files the adjournment.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A bile-green stamp, a sealed stump-ribbon, a constellation sticker of a crab.
pitches.whyNotACopy: Regrowth and the cauterizing trick are ancient. The committee lanyards are the parody. No game-hydra anatomy.

pitches.thaiName: เฮกซะนิบบิ้น
pitches.creatureType: Six-neck strait with a whirlpool partner
pitches.comedyConcept: One side of the door has six necks and a dog's bark. The other side is a whirlpool that inhales the discard pile and burps it back on the wrong turn.
pitches.visualIdentity: A fish-tailed figure in the doorframe with six long necks and a belt of small barking dog-heads. Across the threshold, a mouth in the floor on a tide timer.
pitches.personality: Hexanibble is hungry and precise. The whirlpool is not a person. It is a schedule.
pitches.signatureTrait: Passing close costs six small things, one per neck. Waiting too long means the floor swallows the pile.
pitches.entranceConcept: The corridor narrows until the map is only two bad options.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: Six necks in a single doorway, and a spiral shadow on the opposite tile.
pitches.signatureMechanic: A choice of losses. Dodge the necks and land in the inhale. Time the tide and walk the necks one snack at a time.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: When the whirlpool has eaten enough cards it throws them up as a wave of discarded effects.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: The necks argue over the last boot, knot themselves, and the whirlpool sighs onto a timetable that says CLOSED.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A triple-row tooth, a tide table, one returned card that is slightly damp.
pitches.whyNotACopy: Homer's six heads and twelve feet, plus the thrice-daily swallow, are the sourced bones. The pair is staged as a door and a timetable, not as a scene from a named film.

pitches.thaiName: เพลดจ์ไบเตอร์
pitches.bossTitle: The Wolf on the Rock Clause
pitches.comedyConcept: The tower bound him with a chain braided from a cat's footsteps, a barber's sweepings, and the breath of the cafeteria fish. He bit off the hand that promised to untie him. He is still gagged with a letter-opener.
pitches.visualIdentity: An enormous wolf on a plain rock, muzzled by a sword used as a gag, wrapped in a ridiculous chain of bells, beard-trimmings, and fish bubbles. Not a cinematic armored wolf. Not a god's pet from a franchise.
pitches.personality: He was not born angry. He is angry about the pledge. He keeps the severed handshake like a receipt.
pitches.signatureTrait: While the chain holds, he can only punish oaths. When the last absurd strand snaps, he goes for the leader.
pitches.entranceConcept: The floor is an island of one rock. Every card the party plays that says 'promise' pulls the chain tighter, then frays it.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: A wolf's open jaws stopped by a horizontal blade, a chain made of visibly silly objects.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Oath tension. Binding him is progress and also the thing that frees him. A pledged ally's hand is the first thing he takes.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: The gag breaks. The fight stops being about clauses and becomes a swallow aimed at whoever is standing in front.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: He is not slain like a movie monster. A second figure, only a boot and a shoulder, wedges the jaws and the wolf coughs up the contract. The tower re-ties one strand and looks ashamed.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A chain-link that tinkles like a cat, a bitten signet, a gag-sword that cannot cut anything except promises.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The occult ingredients of the chain, Tyr's bitten pledge, and the sword gag are from Britannica and the Prose Edda. The silhouette is specified against the well-known game and film wolves named in Britannica's Ragnarök article. He is not named Fenrir.

pitches.thaiName: เซเวนเกลร์
pitches.comedyConcept: His face is a lion's grimace stapled to a dragon's mouth, and also, if you squint, a very bad omen read in a sheep's insides. He will hand over his terror if you bring a worse gift.
pitches.visualIdentity: A huge cedar-bark doorman. The face is a clay-mask scowl, not a handsome giant. Seven floating auras, each a different weather, orbit him like name badges.
pitches.personality: Lonely, mountain-born, and furious that Enlil-types keep assigning his radiance to rivers and offices after he is fired.
pitches.signatureTrait: Eye contact is a status. He has seven of them to give away, and each gift makes the room safer and him sadder.
pitches.entranceConcept: The party hears the cedars being counted. He looks up. Everyone's feet stick.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: A mask-wide face, a flood-shaped chest, seven distinct halos.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Seven bribes. Each successful offering removes one aura and one attack. A refused aura hits the whole party. Killing him before the seventh aura makes the tower angry, because the auras have nowhere legal to go.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: At four auras he weeps and the look of death becomes an actual gaze attack. At one aura he is small enough to pity, which is the dangerous part.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: The last aura pops. He sits down, asks to be a neighbor, and is gently reassigned to the reed-beds, the lions, and the lost-and-found. The head stays on.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A clay-mask fragment, one aura in a jar, a cedar splinter that hums when someone lies.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The seven terrors, the look of death, the lion-dragon face, and Enlil's redistribution are from the Sumerian poem. The comedy is bureaucracy and bad gifts, not a game adaptation of Gilgamesh. The defeat does not restage the beheading.

pitches.thaiName: เพสเซิลคอทเทจ
pitches.creatureType: Spinning hut that is also the pilot
pitches.comedyConcept: The boss is the house. It spins on bird legs, commutes by mortar and pestle, and guards a drinking fountain that claims to be the water of life and is mostly very cold tea.
pitches.visualIdentity: A crooked cottage on two chicken legs, a skull-picket fence that is actually labeled coat hooks, an iron kettle used as a helicopter. No child, no oven gag, no kidnapped victim.
pitches.personality: The cottage is house-proud. The pestle is the angry one.
pitches.signatureTrait: The arena rotates continuously. Standing still is how you get dizzy and stamped by a bird foot.
pitches.entranceConcept: A floor that was a forest a moment ago. The hut walks in, sits in the middle, and asks everyone to wipe their feet while turning.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: A hut on two bird legs, a pestle like a mast.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Rotation. Attacks come from whichever wall is currently the front door. Stopping the spin requires offering something that is not a person.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: The hut takes off in the mortar. The fence stays behind and is a much worse conversationalist.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: Someone gives it a better set of legs, or a cup of the cold tea. It curtseys, spins the other way, and parks itself as a secret shop.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: A pestle that stirs weather, a bird-leg doorstop, a thermos of almost-magical tea.
pitches.whyNotACopy: Bird-leg hut, mortar, pestle, and the water of life are the Britannica details that are safe to play with. The ogress who eats children is deliberately not in this pitch. No film Baba Yaga design.

pitches.thaiName: พาร์ตลี่ไลออน
pitches.comedyConcept: A lion front, a goat middle, and a snake tail who filed one body under three names and now refuse to share a throat.
pitches.visualIdentity: The classic lion-goat-serpent arrangement, but each head wears a different tiny hat and they are mid-quarrel. Fire only happens when the goat and the lion shout at the same time. The snake is taking minutes.
pitches.personality: Three personalities, one digestive system. Majority rules, and there is no majority.
pitches.signatureTrait: Each head has its own intent. Damage to one head offends the other two in incompatible ways.
pitches.entranceConcept: They enter as three animals walking abreast, realize they are attached, and blame the doorway.
pitches.signatureSilhouette: Three heads at three heights, three hats, one embarrassed torso.
pitches.signatureMechanic: Vote. The party can bribe one head to abstain. If all three agree, they breathe fire by accident and are furious about it.
pitches.phaseTransformationConcept: The goat tries to secede and the body hops in a circle. The snake calls a point of order.
pitches.defeatAnimationConcept: They agree to be three roommates who happen to share a ribcage, blow out their own flame, and demand separate loot piles.
pitches.uniqueLootTheme: Three tiny hats, a lead-tipped pencil that melts when lied with, a shared stomach-ache coupon.
pitches.whyNotACopy: The body plan is the ancient Lycian monster, which is the recognizable part. The argument and the hats are the character. Bellerophon and Pegasus are not on the card.
